days.title: All the Messengers, or No Faith
days.question: Can someone believe in some messengers and disbelieve in others?
days.principle: Belief in Allah's messengers is inseparable and accepts no division or partiality: whoever disbelieves in one of them has disbelieved in Allah the Exalted and in all His messengers.

misconception.peopleSay: What matters is believing in God; I don't have to believe in all the messengers, I can believe in only some of them.
misconception.correct: Belief in Allah's messengers is inseparable and accepts no division or partiality: whoever disbelieves in one of them has disbelieved in Allah the Exalted and in all His messengers, and those who say "we believe in some and disbelieve in others" are the true disbelievers.

days.action: Reflect on the verse ﴿قُلْ إِن كُنتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي﴾ (Al 'Imran 31), and choose one sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ that you know and do it today as an expression of your love for Allah.
lesson: Allah made obeying the messengers part of faith; the verse ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾ is repeated in Surat ash-Shu'ara' on the tongues of Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb. Obeying the Prophet ﷺ is obeying Allah, and he said that all of his Ummah will enter Paradise except whoever refuses, and the one who refuses is the one who disobeys him. Verse 31 of Al 'Imran judges anyone who claims to love Allah while not following the way of Muhammad ﷺ. Then the book establishes that belief in all the messengers is inseparable: whoever disbelieves in one of them is as if he disbelieved in them all. That is why the Quran says the people of Nuh denied the messengers even though they denied a single messenger, because the religion is one and the One who sent them is one. The believers make no distinction between any of the messengers.
days.quote: It is known that each of those nations denied its own messenger; yet denying one messenger counts as denying all the messengers, given that the religion is one and the Sender is one.

quiz.question: Someone says: "I believe in Musa and 'Isa, but I don't believe in Muhammad ﷺ." What is his ruling?
options: Only a believer with deficient faith
A disbeliever in all the messengers, because disbelieving in one messenger is disbelieving in all
A believer as long as he believes in God
A personal choice with no ruling
quiz.explanation: Yet denying one messenger counts as denying all the messengers, given that the religion is one and the Sender is one.

quiz.question: How does the Quran describe those who say "we believe in some messengers and disbelieve in others"?
options: They are the true disbelievers
Believers who fall short
Sinners
People of legitimate reasoning

quiz.question: What is the relationship between obeying the Prophet ﷺ and entering Paradise?
options: There is none
Paradise is by intention only
Obeying scholars is what enters one into Paradise
Whoever obeys him enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys him has refused

askTheBook: Why must belief in the messengers include all of them?
What is the relationship between obeying the Messenger and obeying Allah?
What does it mean that the people of Nuh denied the messengers?

days.title: The Hour Is Coming, but When?
days.question: Can anyone know when the Day of Resurrection will be? And what are the signs before it?
days.principle: We believe in the portents and signs before the Hour that came in the Quran and the authentic Sunnah, and that knowledge of the Hour is one of the keys of the unseen that no one knows except Allah.

misconception.peopleSay: Some people can calculate and fix the exact date of the Day of Resurrection.
misconception.correct: Knowledge of the Hour is one of the keys of the unseen that no one knows except Allah. When the Prophet ﷺ was asked about it, he said: «ما المسؤول عنها بأعلم من السائل».

days.action: Read verse 34 of Surat Luqman and find the five things whose knowledge Allah kept to Himself, and think about how this makes you prepare through deeds instead of being preoccupied with the date.
lesson: Belief in the Last Day begins with affirming the signs that come before the Hour, as they came in the Quran and the authentic Sunnah. But the time of the Hour itself is one of the keys of the unseen that only Allah knows. Even the Prophet ﷺ, when Jibril asked him about it, said that the one asked knows no more than the one asking. The Hour will come suddenly, but before it there are minor signs, such as the taking away of knowledge, the spread of trials and indecency, much killing and earthquakes. Among the signs is also the appearance of nearly thirty lying impostors, each claiming to be a messenger. And wealth will increase until its owner looks for someone to accept his charity and finds no one.
days.quote: And He made clear that the Hour comes suddenly, and that before it there are portents and signs.

quiz.question: Someone posted on social media that he has calculated the date of the Hour. Do we believe him?
options: Maybe, if his calculation is precise
We believe him if he's a sheikh
No, knowledge of the Hour is part of the unseen that no one knows except Allah
We believe him if all the signs have appeared
quiz.explanation: And that knowledge of the Hour is one of the keys of the unseen that no one knows except Allah.

quiz.question: When Jibril asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Hour, what does his answer teach us?
options: That the Prophet ﷺ knew it but didn't say
That even the greatest of creation do not know its time
That the Hour will not come
That the angels know it

quiz.question: If the Hour comes suddenly, what is the benefit of the signs before it?
options: A warning for people to prepare, without fixing the time
They fix the exact day
They have no benefit at all
They postpone the Hour
quiz.explanation: And He made clear that the Hour comes suddenly, and that before it there are portents and signs.

askTheBook: Who knows the time of the Day of Resurrection?
What are the minor signs of the Hour?
What are the five things whose knowledge Allah kept to Himself in Surat Luqman?

days.title: The Trial of the False Messiah (al-Masih ad-Dajjal)
days.question: Who is the False Messiah, and how would I recognise him if he appeared?
days.principle: Among the major signs of the Hour is the emergence of the False Messiah, a person with whom Allah tests His servants at the end of time. He claims divinity, then Allah renders him powerless, voids his affair, and 'Isa, peace be upon him, kills him.

misconception.peopleSay: If someone can perform wonders, like commanding the sky to rain or bringing the dead to life, he must be on the truth.
misconception.correct: Allah enables the Dajjal to do some of the things within His power as a test, such as commanding the sky to rain and it rains, and reviving a dead man he has killed. All of that happens by Allah's power and will; then Allah renders him powerless, voids his affair, and 'Isa, peace be upon him, kills him.

days.action: The Prophet ﷺ said in the hadith: «فمن أدركه منكم فليقرأ عليه فواتح سورة الكهف». Read the opening verses of Surat al-Kahf today and learn their meanings.
lesson: The first major sign the book discusses is the Dajjal, who will appear at the end of time as a severe test for people and will claim to be a god. Allah enables him to do things that tempt people, such as commanding the sky to rain and the earth to grow plants, with the treasures of the earth following him. But all of this is by Allah's power and will, and in the end Allah renders him powerless and 'Isa, peace be upon him, kills him. Allah placed two signs in his face that expose his lie: he is one-eyed, and between his eyes is written "kafir" (disbeliever), which every believer can read. The Prophet ﷺ said he will remain forty days: a day like a year, a day like a month, a day like a week, and the rest of his days like ours. When the Companions asked about prayer on the day like a year, he told them to estimate its measure.
days.quote: Allah has placed in the face of the Dajjal two signs that testify to his lying and his disbelief.

quiz.question: The Dajjal will do extraordinary things, like commanding the sky to rain. Does that mean he has power of his own?
options: Yes, it proves his divinity
Yes, he has independent power
It is magic he can do by himself
No, it is a test by Allah's power and will, and in the end Allah renders him powerless
quiz.explanation: Allah has placed in the face of the Dajjal two signs that testify to his lying and his disbelief.

quiz.question: What signs expose the Dajjal's lie to any believer?
options: That he is very tall
That he speaks many languages
That he is one-eyed, and "kafir" is written between his eyes
That he only comes out at night
quiz.explanation: The first: he is one-eyed; the second: "kafir" is written between his eyes.

quiz.question: During the Dajjal's long days (a day like a year), how is prayer performed?
options: Five prayers suffice for the whole day
We estimate its measure, i.e. we calculate the prayer times
Prayer is dropped
We pray only when the sun sets

askTheBook: Who is the False Messiah?
What signs expose the Dajjal?
How long will the Dajjal remain on earth?

days.title: The Descent of 'Isa and the Remaining Major Signs
days.question: Will 'Isa, peace be upon him, come down again? And what will he do when he does?
days.principle: Among the major signs of the Hour are the descent of 'Isa son of Maryam, following the Messenger of Islam and ruling by his law; the emergence of Gog and Magog; the rising of the sun from the west; and then a fire coming out of Yemen that drives people to their place of gathering.

misconception.peopleSay: Repentance and faith are accepted at any time, even after the sun rises from the west.
misconception.correct: The rising of the sun from the west closes the door of repentance at that time: when it rises and people see it, they will all believe, and that is when a soul's faith will not benefit it if it had not believed before.

days.action: Do not delay repenting from a sin you are committing, because the book says the door of repentance will close when the sun rises from the west; begin today with sincere seeking of forgiveness.
lesson: Among the major signs is the descent of 'Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him. He will come down following the Messenger of Islam ﷺ and ruling by his law, and this will prove false those who worshipped him besides Allah. The Prophet ﷺ said he will descend as a just judge: he will break the cross, kill the pig and abolish the jizyah, and wealth will overflow until no one accepts it. The hadiths about his descent are mass-transmitted (mutawatir), and he is the one who will kill the Dajjal. After that, among the major signs are the emergence of Gog and Magog and the rising of the sun from the west, at which point the door of repentance closes. The last of the signs is a fire coming out of Yemen that drives people to their gathering place in the land of Sham.
days.quote: The hadiths from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are mass-transmitted that he foretold the descent of 'Isa, peace be upon him, before the Day of Resurrection as a just leader and an equitable judge.

quiz.question: When 'Isa, peace be upon him, descends at the end of time, by which law will he rule?
options: By the law of Islam, following our master Muhammad ﷺ
By a new law
By the Gospel
By the law of Musa
quiz.explanation: The descent of 'Isa son of Maryam, following the Messenger of Islam and ruling by his law.

quiz.question: Someone says: "I'll wait until I see the major signs of the Hour and then repent." Is that sound thinking?
options: Yes, repentance is open at any time, even after them
Yes, the signs give a bigger chance
The signs have nothing to do with repentance
No, the rising of the sun from the west closes the door of repentance
quiz.explanation: And Allah the Exalted said, referring to the rising of the sun from the west and the closing of the door of repentance at that time…

quiz.question: Is the descent of 'Isa, peace be upon him, based on weak, singly-narrated hadiths?
options: Yes, and we don't have to believe them
There are no hadiths at all
No, the hadiths about his descent are mass-transmitted (mutawatir)
It is only the opinion of some scholars
quiz.explanation: The hadiths from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are mass-transmitted that he foretold the descent of 'Isa, peace be upon him, before the Day of Resurrection as a just leader and an equitable judge.

askTheBook: What will 'Isa, peace be upon him, do when he descends?
What are the major signs of the Hour?
When does the door of repentance close?

days.title: The First Station of the Hereafter: The Grave
days.question: What happens to a person in his grave after he is buried?
days.principle: We believe in what happens in the grave of questioning, bliss and punishment; the texts of the two revelations agree in affirming it, and the Salaf and the imams across the centuries agreed on it.

misconception.peopleSay: There is no such thing as questioning or punishment in the grave; all of that is after the Day of Resurrection.
misconception.correct: The texts of the two revelations, Quran and Sunnah, agree in affirming what happens in the grave of questioning, trial, bliss and punishment, and the Salaf agreed on it. The verse of Surat Ghafir indicates the punishment of the grave, because being exposed to the Fire morning and evening happens before the Day of Resurrection.

days.action: Ask yourself today the questions the two angels ask about the Prophet ﷺ, and think: does my life confirm my answer that he is Allah's servant and messenger?
lesson: Part of belief in the Last Day is believing in what happens in the grave of questioning, bliss and punishment, and the Salaf and the imams agreed on this. The verse ﴿يُثَبِّتُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِالْقَوْلِ الثَّابِتِ﴾ refers to being made firm at the time of questioning in the grave. The verse about Pharaoh's people indicates the punishment of the grave, because they are exposed to the Fire morning and evening before the Day of Resurrection. The Prophet ﷺ related that the dead person hears the footsteps of his companions as they walk away, and then two angels come, sit him up and ask him about the Prophet ﷺ. The believer says: I bear witness that he is Allah's servant and messenger, and he is shown his seat in the Fire that Allah has replaced with a seat in Paradise. As for the hypocrite and the disbeliever, he says: I don't know; I used to say what people said.
days.quote: The texts of the two revelations, Quran and Sunnah, agree in affirming what happens in the grave of questioning, trial, bliss and punishment.

quiz.question: Someone says: "The punishment of the grave has no evidence." What is the correct understanding?
options: He is right
It is established by the texts of the Quran and Sunnah and the consensus of the Salaf
It is established only by weak Sunnah
A disputed, unimportant matter
quiz.explanation: The texts of the two revelations, Quran and Sunnah, agree in affirming what happens in the grave of questioning, trial, bliss and punishment.

quiz.question: How does the verse about Pharaoh's people indicate the punishment of the grave?
options: Because their exposure to the Fire morning and evening is before the Day of Resurrection
Because it speaks only about the Day of Resurrection
It has nothing to do with the grave
Because it speaks about this world
quiz.explanation: Because the exposure to the Fire morning and evening happens before the Day of Resurrection.

quiz.question: When the believer is asked in his grave about the Prophet ﷺ, how does he answer?
options: He cannot answer
He says: I heard people saying something
He stays silent
He bears witness that he is Allah's servant and messenger

askTheBook: What happens in the grave?
What is the evidence from the Quran for the punishment of the grave?
What do the two angels ask the dead person about?

days.title: We Will Rise Again, Certainly
days.question: How will people come back after they die and become dust?
days.principle: Belief in the Resurrection after death is one of the dividing lines between faith and heresy; the explicit Quran and Sunnah prove it, and the Muslims are agreed upon it.

misconception.peopleSay: It's impossible for bones to come back after becoming dust.
misconception.correct: «قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة». Allah argued from His power to begin creation to His power to repeat it, which is even easier for Him, and argued from reviving the dead earth to reviving the dead.

days.action: Memorise the supplication the Prophet ﷺ used to teach the Companions as he would teach them a surah of the Quran («اللهم إني أعوذ بك من عذاب جهنم...») and say it today.
lesson: The book closes its discussion of the grave with the supplication the Prophet ﷺ used to teach the Companions as he would teach a surah of the Quran, which includes seeking refuge from the punishment of the grave. Then it begins speaking about the Day of Resurrection, starting with the Resurrection itself. Belief in the Resurrection is the difference between faith and heresy, and the Muslims and the followers of all the messages agreed on it. Some people went astray on this: some denied both creation and return, some believed in creation but denied the return, and some said only souls will return. The Quran answered them with clear examples: the One who revives the dead earth with rain is able to revive the dead, and for the One who began creation the first time, repeating it is easier.
days.quote: As for the Resurrection after death, belief in it is one of the dividing lines between faith and heresy.

quiz.question: Someone says: "How will Allah bring back bones after they decompose?" What is the Quran's answer?
options: It is rationally impossible
That is metaphorical, not real
The One who created them the first time is able to revive them again
Only the soul is resurrected

quiz.question: What evidence for the Resurrection do we see every year?
options: There is no tangible evidence
Dead land that Allah revives with rain
The movement of the stars
Only the change of seasons
quiz.explanation: His arguing from His power to revive the dead earth to reviving the dead.

quiz.question: Someone says he is a Muslim but isn't convinced of the Resurrection. What is his ruling?
options: Belief in the Resurrection divides faith from heresy, so denying it takes one out of faith
An ordinary Muslim
It's a personal opinion
A Muslim who falls short
quiz.explanation: Belief in it is one of the dividing lines between faith and heresy.

askTheBook: Why is belief in the Resurrection important?
Who are the people who went astray regarding the Resurrection?
What evidence from the Quran is there for the Resurrection?

days.title: The Gathering, the Presentation and the Reckoning
days.question: How will people be gathered on the Day of Resurrection? And will everyone be judged the same way?
days.principle: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked and uncircumcised. Then comes the presentation before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which is of two kinds, general and specific. As for the reckoning, it is close examination, and whoever is closely examined will be punished.
days.action: The Prophet ﷺ said: «فاتقوا النار ولو بشق تمرة». Give some charity today, even something small.
lesson: After the Resurrection, people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, and the Quran, Sunnah and consensus indicate this. When Aisha was surprised that men and women would look at one another, the Prophet ﷺ told her that the matter will be too severe for that. Then comes the presentation before Allah, which is of two kinds: a general presentation of all creatures in which nothing is hidden, and a specific presentation for the believers. In the specific presentation, Allah makes the believer acknowledge his sins and tells him: I concealed them for you in the world and I forgive them for you today. As for the reckoning, it is close examination, and the Prophet ﷺ said whoever is closely examined will be punished. Allah will speak to each person without an interpreter, and he will see nothing but what he sent ahead.
days.quote: The general presentation: the presentation of all creatures before their Lord, their records laid open before Him; nothing of them is hidden from Him.

quiz.question: Someone says: "On the Day of Resurrection everyone will be judged in the same way." What does the book say?
options: He is right
There is no reckoning at all
The reckoning is only for disbelievers
Whoever is closely examined in his reckoning is punished, and there are people Allah conceals

quiz.question: To the believer who concealed his sins in this world, what does Allah say on the Day of Resurrection?
options: I will expose you before people
There is no forgiveness
I concealed them for you in the world and I forgive them for you today
You must be punished first

quiz.question: In the general presentation on the Day of Resurrection, can anyone hide anything?
options: Yes, whoever can hide something will
No, all creatures are presented to their Lord and nothing of them is hidden from Him
Only disbelievers are presented
Each person presents what he wants
quiz.explanation: The general presentation: the presentation of all creatures before their Lord, their records laid open before Him; nothing of them is hidden from Him.

askTheBook: How will people be gathered on the Day of Resurrection?
What are the kinds of presentation before Allah?
What is the difference between the presentation and the reckoning?

days.title: The Record, the Scale, the Bridge and the Basin
days.question: What stations will a person pass through on the Day of Resurrection after the reckoning?
days.principle: The record of deeds will be placed, containing the great and the small; the scales will be set up, and whoever's scales are heavy will be saved and whoever's scales are light will perish; the Sirat is a bridge stretched over Hell that all people will cross according to their deeds; and al-Kawthar is a basin Allah gave our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
days.action: Say often today «سبحان الله وبحمده، سبحان الله العظيم», the two phrases the Prophet ﷺ said are heavy on the scale.
lesson: On the Day of Resurrection the record of deeds will be placed, containing everything great and small, and the criminals will be afraid of what is in it. The witnesses are the guardian angels and the noble scribes, as well as a person's hearing, sight, skin and all his limbs. The Prophet ﷺ laughed as he told of a servant who argues with his Lord and wants a witness from himself; Allah seals his mouth and his limbs speak of his deeds. Then the scales are set up: whoever's scales are heavy is saved and whoever's scales are light perishes. The Sirat is a bridge over Hell, and on it some are saved unharmed, some are saved but scratched, and some fall into the Fire. After that is al-Kawthar, the basin Allah gave the Prophet ﷺ; its water is whiter than snow and sweeter than honey, and whoever drinks from it will never thirst again.
days.quote: The record is the record of deeds, and it contains the great and the small.

quiz.question: Someone says: "Nobody records these small sins." What is the correct understanding?
options: The record of deeds contains the great and the small
He is right
Minor sins are wiped away by themselves
Only major sins are recorded
quiz.explanation: The record is the record of deeds, and it contains the great and the small.

quiz.question: Who will testify against a person on the Day of Resurrection?
options: No one testifies
Only the people who knew him
Only he testifies against himself
The guardian angels, and also his hearing, sight, skin and limbs
quiz.explanation: The witnesses are the guardian angels and the noble scribes, and they are also the hearing, the sight, the skin and all the limbs.

quiz.question: Who crosses the Sirat?
options: Only the disbelievers
Only the righteous
All people come to it and cross according to their deeds
No one crosses it
quiz.explanation: The Sirat is a bridge stretched over Hell.

askTheBook: Who will testify against a person on the Day of Resurrection?
What is the Sirat?
What is the description of the Prophet's ﷺ basin?

days.title: Intercession, by Allah's Permission
days.question: Can anyone intercede for anyone on the Day of Resurrection?
days.principle: Intercession is established with its two conditions: Allah's permission for the intercessor to intercede, and His being pleased with the one interceded for; so all of it goes back to Him.

misconception.peopleSay: I can choose anyone myself to be my intercessor with Allah, and he will simply intercede for me.
misconception.correct: Intercession is established with two conditions: Allah's permission for the intercessor and His being pleased with the one interceded for, so all of it goes back to Him. Allah condemned the polytheists who took intercessors besides Him on their own initiative, without evidence or proof.

days.action: When you hear the adhan today, say afterwards the supplication in the hadith: «اللهم رب هذه الدعوة التامة والصلاة القائمة آت محمداً الوسيلة والفضيلة وابعثه مقاماً محموداً الذي وعدته».
lesson: Intercession on the Day of Resurrection is true, but it has two conditions: Allah permits the intercessor to intercede, and He is pleased with the one interceded for. So all intercession ultimately goes back to Allah, and no one can take intercessors on his own. The greatest intercession is the Supreme Intercession: the praised station Allah promised the Prophet ﷺ, when he intercedes for the people standing on that Day so that judgement may be passed between them. The Prophet ﷺ also has an intercession for opening the gate of Paradise; he is its first intercessor, and its keeper tells him he was ordered not to open it for anyone before him. There is intercession for the sinners among the monotheists, and this is also for the angels, the prophets and the righteous. The happiest of people with the Prophet's ﷺ intercession is whoever said "There is no god but Allah" sincerely from his heart.
days.quote: Meaning: all creatures and their Creator, Blessed and Exalted, will praise you in it; it is the Supreme Intercession that Allah reserved for our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

quiz.question: Someone says: "This saint will intercede for me on the Day of Resurrection even if Allah is not pleased with me." Is that right?
options: Right, saints intercede for anyone
No, intercession has two conditions: Allah's permission for the intercessor and His being pleased with the one interceded for
Right, if he visits him often
Right, if he loves him
quiz.explanation: It is established with its two conditions: Allah's permission for the intercessor to intercede, and His being pleased with the one interceded for.

quiz.question: Does the Supreme Intercession on the Day of Resurrection belong to any prophet?
options: No, it is exclusive to our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
To all the prophets
To the angels
To the righteous
quiz.explanation: Among them is the Supreme Intercession, which is exclusive to our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

quiz.question: A monotheist Muslim committed sins and entered the Fire. Can he come out through intercession?
options: No, whoever enters the Fire never leaves
Intercession is only for disbelievers
Intercession is only for the righteous
Yes, there is intercession for the sinners among the monotheists
quiz.explanation: Among them is his intercession for the sinners among the monotheists, and this last one is also for the angels, the prophets and the righteous.

askTheBook: What are the conditions of intercession?
What is the Supreme Intercession?
Who is happiest with the Prophet's ﷺ intercession?

days.title: Paradise and Hellfire
days.question: Do Paradise and Hellfire exist now? And will they ever come to an end?
days.principle: Paradise and Hellfire have been prepared and already brought into existence, and we believe in their permanence and continuance by Allah's keeping them; they will never perish, nor will those in them.

misconception.peopleSay: Paradise and Hellfire will only be created on the Day of Resurrection.
misconception.correct: Paradise and Hellfire have been prepared and already brought into existence, and the Quran points to this by saying of Paradise «أعدت للمتقين» and of the Fire «أعدت للكافرين».

days.action: Read verse 133 of Al 'Imran («وسارعوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم») and choose one good deed to hasten to today.
lesson: Part of belief in the Last Day is believing that Paradise and Hellfire actually exist now, and that they remain by Allah's keeping them and will never perish. The Quran said of Paradise that it is prepared for the God-fearing, and of the Fire that it is prepared for the disbelievers, meaning they are already made ready. The Prophet ﷺ related that death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection in the form of a ram and slaughtered, and it will be said to the people of Paradise: eternity, no death; and to the people of the Fire: eternity, no death. Allah has prepared for the righteous in Paradise what no eye has seen, no ear has heard and no human heart has imagined. The first group to enter Paradise will have faces like the moon on the night of the full moon, and it will be announced that they will remain young and never grow old. As for the fire of this world, it is one part of seventy parts of the fire of Hell.

quiz.question: Someone says: "Paradise and Hellfire will only be created on the Day of Resurrection." What is the correct understanding?
options: He is right
They don't exist at all
They already exist and are prepared now
Only the Fire exists
quiz.explanation: And that they have been prepared and already brought into existence.

quiz.question: Do Paradise and Hellfire have an end?
options: Yes, they perish after a while
No, they remain by Allah's keeping them and never perish
Paradise remains and the Fire perishes
No one knows

quiz.question: The fire of this world that we know: how does it compare to the fire of Hell?
options: It is one part of seventy parts of it
It is exactly like it
It is more intense
It has no relation to it

askTheBook: Do Paradise and Hellfire exist now?
How are the people of Paradise described in the hadiths?
How hot is the fire of Hell compared with the fire of this world?
